mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: higher rates predict negative 20-day returns due to increased discount rates on equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is above 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy phase that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 4.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0% and industrial production (INDPRO) is below 100, it indicates a tight labor market and supply chain stress, which together predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply constraints
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE<=4.0 AND INDPRO<=100 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP level above 23500 billion dollars and unemployment rate below 4.0%), a positive demand shock (measured by RSAFS above 700,000) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1>23500 AND UNRATE<4.0 AND RSAFS>700000 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
